message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and niche horror films that have earned a reputation for being genuinely scary or unsettling:

| # | Title | Year | Why it’s worth watching |
|---|-------|------|------------------------|
| 1 | **The Shining** | 1980 | A masterclass in psychological dread, with an iconic performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 2 | **Hereditary** | 2018 | A brutal, family‑driven horror that blends supernatural terror with real‑world grief. |
| 3 | **The Exorcist** | 1973 | The quintessential exorcism film that still feels fresh and deeply unsettling. |
| 4 | **Get Out** | 2017 | A smart, socially conscious horror that mixes satire with genuine scares. |
| 5 | **A Quiet Place** | 2018 | Tension built around silence; a fresh take on the “survival horror” genre. |
| 6 | **Midsommar** | 2019 | A daylight horror that turns the idyllic Swedish festival into a nightmare. |
| 7 | **It Follows** | 2014 | A modern folk‑tale of a curse that’s both creepy and conceptually unique. |
| 8 | **The Babadook** | 2014 | A psychological horror that uses a monster as a metaphor for grief. |
| 9 | **The Ring** (Japanese original) | 1998 | A chilling, atmospheric ghost‑story that spawned a successful Hollywood remake. |
|10 | **The Witch** | 2015 | A slow‑burn, period‑piece horror that relies on atmosphere and dread. |
|11 | **Paranormal Activity** | 2007 | Low‑budget found‑footage that made the genre feel immediate and personal. |
|12 | **The Conjuring** | 2013 | A modern classic that blends folklore with a strong narrative. |
|13 | **Suspiria** (2018) | 2018 | A visually striking remake that amps up the supernatural terror. |
|14 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | 2012 | A meta‑take that subverts horror tropes while still delivering genuine scares. |
|15 | **The Others** | 2001 | A gothic thriller that keeps you guessing until the very end. |

Feel free to pick based on your taste—whether you prefer psychological dread, supernatural chills, or a blend of both. Enjoy the fright!
